status_note: The mathematical claims below are derivations in report.md, not externally peer-reviewed results. Literature entries are context, not validation of these exact formulations.

claims.claim: For loss in [0,1], |R_Q(h)-R_P(h)| <= TV(P,Q), and the bound is sharp.
assumptions: P and Q are joint distributions on representation-label pairs
claims.evidence: Variational TV inequality; indicator loss on a TV-maximizing event gives equality.

claims.claim: Target excess of any source predictor is at most source excess + min(2 TV(P,Q),1); the shift term is sharp as a supremum.
assumptions: same hypothesis class is evaluated on both domains
claims.evidence: Three-term risk decomposition and a binary two-hypothesis construction.

claims.claim: Finite-class source ERM from n iid source labels has target excess <= min(1, 2 sqrt(log(2M/alpha)/(2n)) + 2 delta) with probability >= 1-alpha, where delta=TV(P,Q).
Oracle importance-weighted ERM under target support coverage and bounded ratio has target excess <= min(1, 2 sqrt(2 kappa t/n) + 4 B t/(3n)), with kappa=1+chi-square(Q_Z||P_Z) and t=log(2M/alpha).
assumptions: common conditional label law given acquired Z=phi(X)
Q_Z absolutely continuous with respect to P_Z
known ratio w=dQ_Z/dP_Z bounded by B
claims.evidence: Importance-weight identity, Var(w loss)<=E_P[w^2], two-sided Bernstein and union bound.

claims.claim: For an independent fixed estimated ratio, target excess incurs an additional 2 E_P|w_tilde-w| term, plus a weighted empirical-process term based on E_P[w_tilde^2] and its bound.
assumptions: estimated ratio is independent of the labeled sample
claims.evidence: For each predictor, |E_P[(w_tilde-w) loss]| <= E_P|w_tilde-w|, then apply ERM comparison twice.

claims.claim: If target mass rho lies outside source support and labels there are unknown, unlabeled target covariates cannot guarantee target risk below rho/2 in the worst case for randomized predictors; deterministic predictors incur rho in one of two label worlds.
assumptions: two target label worlds agree on all observed source labels and target covariates but differ on A
claims.report_section: Why support and conditional invariance are load-bearing

claims.claim: Equal source and target representation marginals do not ensure low target risk if the conditional label law changes.
assumptions: binary feature Z with uniform marginal in both domains
source label Y=1-Z and target label Y=Z
claims.evidence: Source ERM's perfect source rule has target 0-1 error one.
claims.report_section: Why support and conditional invariance are load-bearing

claims.claim: Primary literature treats target/source divergence and shared target competence as transfer conditions, and documents that covariate shift or unlabeled target samples alone do not settle adaptation.
evidence: Ben-David et al., AISTATS 2010, Impossibility Theorems for Domain Adaptation: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v9/david10a.html
Ben-David et al., Machine Learning 79 (2010), A Theory of Learning from Different Domains: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10994-009-5152-4
